prompt: Explain inflation using only tailgating metaphors. Do not stop when the metaphors break down.
response:
Inflation is when the parking lot gets so packed that your prime spot by the stadium gate now costs three cases of premium lager instead of one, and even then, you’re still parked behind a dumpster. The parking attendant (the central bank) tries to manage the flow by raising the entry fee, hoping fewer cars will show up, but everyone’s already committed to the party and just grumbles while digging deeper into their coolers.

Your dollar bill is a red plastic cup. At the start of the season, that cup held a generous pour of domestic draft. Now, the keg is running warm and the guy pouring is skimping, so that same cup only gets you a lukewarm splash of light beer. You need two cups just to feel the buzz you used to get from one, but the line for the tap has doubled in length because everyone else is also holding out multiple cups.

The price of charcoal briquettes is your consumer price index. Last year, a bag got your grill to searing temp for four quarters of bratwurst. This year, that same bag only burns hot enough for two quarters of hot dogs, so you have to buy three bags to finish the pre-game menu. The butcher sees the charcoal shortage and marks up the brats, and the guy selling buns sees the brat markup and raises his prices, creating a supply chain of tailgate misery where every vendor is just passing the burn down the line.

Wage growth is showing up late to the lot with a smaller cooler. Your buddy who brings the expensive steaks (your paycheck) hasn’t upgraded his haul in years, but the cost of ice, napkins, and folding chairs keeps climbing. So now, instead of ribeyes, he’s bringing generic sliders, and everyone’s pretending it’s fine while secretly calculating how many sliders equal one steak from last season. The tailgate feels more expensive not because the party got better, but because the same spread requires twice the grocery run.
